label: Lanino & Elnina
_shapeNote: UNUSUAL SHAPE — READ THIS BEFORE WIRING IT UP. (1) `enemy` is deliberately the CONTROLLER, not a monster. obj_lanino_enemy and obj_elnina_enemy are the two visible monsterparent enemies (scr_encountersetup.gml:709-716, encounter 113) but neither of them contains one line of attack code: their Step events are 133 lines of ACT dialogue and nothing else. obj_elnina_enemy_Create_0.gml:25 does `instance_create(x, y, obj_elnina_lanino_controller);` and that controller owns the whole fight. Both the boxBlock and the turnBlock read `turns`, a controller variable, so they MUST be replayed with self = an obj_elnina_lanino_controller instance or they throw. (2) There is NO `monsterattackname` anywhere in this fight — not in either enemy, not in the controller, not in the type-130 branch of obj_dbulletcontroller. gen_attacks.js's announcement scan finds ZERO attacks for this boss no matter which object you put in `enemy`; the roster below is declared, not scanned. (3) selectorScan is NOT applicable either: this is not Ch1-style `if (var == N) spawn`. The dispatcher is a single unconditional `dc.type = 130` and the attack is chosen by a second field, `dc.special`, off a turn ladder. Scanning `turns == N` over the controller Step would hit 40+ dialogue branches and produce garbage.

mechanics:
ONE FIGHT, TWO ENEMIES, ONE CONTROLLER, ONE ATTACK SHAPE.

Encounter 113 (scr_encountersetup.gml:702-725): obj_lanino_enemy (monstertype 61, line 709) at view +480/+46 and obj_elnina_enemy (monstertype 60, line 713) at +510/+180, rank1turns 7 (line 719). obj_elnina_enemy_Create_0.gml:25 spawns obj_elnina_lanino_controller, which does everything: intro, forecast UI, turn ladder, the single dispatcher, all post-bullet dialogue, and the win. The two enemy objects contain no attack code at all — their Steps (gml_Object_obj_lanino_enemy_Step_0.gml:15-109 and the mirror-image obj_elnina_enemy_Step_0.gml:15-109) are pure ACT handling, and every ACT writes back into the controller.

WIN CONDITION IS NOT HP. Tenna announces it in the intro (Step_0:110-124): say "I LOVE TV" 99 times. Susie's and Ralsei's S-Action/R-Action slots are renamed "ILoveTV" while the controller exists (scr_spellmenu_setup.gml:50-51 and 74-75). Each ACT bumps `ilovetv_increase`, and Step_0:189-222 ticks the counter up one per frame with a rising pitch. The counter is HARD-CAPPED AT 30 for most of the fight: Step_0:210-211, `if (ilovetvlimit == true && ilovetv == 40) ilovetv = 30;` — you literally cannot win early. `ilovetvlimit` is only cleared at Step_0:2115, inside the scripted ending, and Step_0:2124-2132 then sets `ilovetv_increase = 99` so the counter races to 99 on its own while obj_ilovetv balloons spawn (2143-2156). Then scr_wincombat() at 2186. The battle is therefore ALWAYS won on the script, never on damage.

THE TURN LADDER (the chooser). `turns` (Create_0:3 = 0) increments once per enemy turn at Step_0:332. Two regulators sit on it:
  * Step_0:235-237 (menu phase) — `else if (turns > 1 && ilovetv == 0 && turn2_turns < 7) turns = 0;`. If the player has not said I LOVE TV even once, the ladder is pinned to turn 1 for up to seven menu phases. Special 0 repeats.
  * Step_0:230-233 (menu) and 334-335 (enemytalk) — once `ilovetv > 0 && turn2_turns > 2`, `turns` is fast-forwarded to 2 and then to 3, skipping ahead to the choicer turn.
The resulting sequence is turns 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> ending, i.e. specials 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 4. There is NO randomness in attack selection anywhere in this fight.

THE DISPATCHER (one site, Step_0:1078-1178). At `rtimer == 12` in the bullets phase it runs `with (_a) { dc = scr_bulletspawner(x, y, obj_dbulletcontroller); dc.type = 130; ... }`. `_a` is 379, falling back to 946 if obj_lanino_enemy is gone (Step_0:1117-1120) — these are raw object indices: objects.tsv line 381 is obj_lanino_enemy (381 - 2 = 379) and line 948 is obj_elnina_enemy (946). So the spawner runs with self = Lanino, or Elnina if Lanino is dead. Only two fields vary: `dc.special` off the turn ladder (1127-1149) and `dc.side` off favouritism (1151-1154). `difficulty` is never written, so it stays 0 (obj_dbulletcontroller_Create_0.gml:21).

TYPE 130 IS A THIN WRAPPER. gml_Object_obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:2614-2624 immediately creates obj_elnina_mascotattack with `attacktype = special`, `favored = side`, `type = difficulty`, then 2626-2627 `if (special != 4) exit;`. All five attacks are branches of obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml (456 lines); the only thing the dbulletcontroller keeps for itself is the final attack's dialogue timing (2629-2746).

FAVOURITISM (`side` / `favored`). Step_0:304: `_lanino_favored = (lastchosen == "" && sunboost > 0) || lastchosen == "lanino"`. Before the turn-3 choicer, `lastchosen` is "" and favouritism is driven purely by ACTs: saying I LOVE TV to Lanino does `sunboost++` capped at 3 (obj_lanino_enemy_Step_0.gml:32-33 and 65-66), to Elnina `sunboost--` floored at -3 (obj_elnina_enemy_Step_0.gml:32-33 and 65-66). After the bullets of turn 3 the game asks outright — a two-option choicer, "#Rain" vs "#Shine" (Step_0:1508-1530) — and the answer LOCKS favouritism for the rest of the fight (Step_0:1531-1590: sunboost -/+3, `lastchosen` "elnina"/"lanino", mirrored into global.flag[1017]). Both sides are reachable for every special, so the real roster is 5 attacks x 2 sides.

THE FORECAST DECIDES BULLET SPRITES, NOT ATTACKS. Step_0:224-300 (menu phase) fills `forecasts[0..2]` with `[temperature, laninoSprite, elninaSprite]` from a switch on `forecast_turn`: turn 0 -> moon+snow, 1 -> sun+rain, 2 -> moon+rain, 3+ -> `choose(0,1)` between sun+snow and moon+rain, with temperatures that run away (80 + 100*(t-3) if Lanino was chosen, 40 - 30*(t-3) if Elnina was). Sprite ids: sun 783, moon 1474, rain 4255, snow 1650 (= spr_weather_sun / _moon / _rain / _snow). obj_elnina_mascotattack_Create_0.gml:11-16 reads forecasts[0] but ONLY while `turns < 7`, and Step_0:305-321 uses it to pick each side's bullet sprite: Lanino moon -> bs[4] spr_ch3_bullet_moon, Lanino sun -> bs[3] spr_ch3_bullet_sun, Elnina rain -> bs[5] spr_ch3_bullet_raindrop, Elnina snow -> bs[1] spr_ch3_bullet_ice. On turn 7 the forecast is skipped and the defaults apply (`bs[3 - i*2]`: Lanino sun, Elnina ice). The dialogue that names the weather ("... Moon." / "... Drop." / "TRUEST Crystal!", Step_0:646-1020) matches the forecast — but it only picks a SPRITE. It also writes `lanino_attack` / `elnina_attack` to 68/69/70/71, which nothing reads (see the cut list).

DIFFICULTY IS A SPRITE OVERRIDE, NOT A DIFFICULTY. obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:293-303 maps `type` (= the dbulletcontroller's `difficulty`) 1/2/3/4 onto bs[5]/bs[1]/bs[4]/bs[3]. The main fight never sets it, so it is 0 and the forecast override wins. The REMATCH is the code path that actually uses it (see below). If the studio's DIFF selector feeds a non-zero difficulty into a main-fight launch, the bullets silently change species.

LOSS COUNTER MAKES IT EASIER. obj_elnina_lanino_controller_Create_0.gml:58-61 increments global.elninalosscount on every fight after the first; obj_elnina_mascotattack_Create_0.gml:9 copies it into `extrabulletrate`, which is ADDED to shotrate (the frames between shots) for specials 2, 3 and 4 — so every retry fires more slowly.

NO SOUL MODE, NO MINIGAME. scr_moveheart() at Step_0:1058-1059 is the plain red soul; obj_growtangle is created with no maxxscale/maxyscale override, so it is the default 2x2 box (obj_growtangle_Create_0.gml:12-13), only its Y position changes on turn 7. There is no green/purple/yellow mode, no obj_purplecontrols, no ACT minigame. Damage is flat: obj_regularbullet_elnina_Create_0.gml:7-8, damage 60 / grazepoints 2.

BULLET-VS-BULLET IS THE FIGHT'S IDENTITY. obj_regularbullet_elnina_Step_0.gml:31-81 does a manual collision_rectangle against its own object each step. Same sprite -> pass through. spr_lanino_fire -> pass through. While `obj_elnina_lanino_controller.turns <= 2` a Lanino bullet meeting an Elnina bullet becomes a pink spr_ch3_bullet_heart (line 46-54) — the couple is in love. From turn 3 on, the same collision annihilates both with a bump and a grey shrink-ball (56-81) — the couple is fighting. Separately, obj_elnina_mascotattack counts its own shots and turns every `firebulletcount`-th bullet into a red 2x spr_lanino_fire (obj_elnina_mascotattack_Create_0.gml:26 sets it to 2000, Step_0:339-348 applies it); in the main fight it is never lowered, so it effectively never fires — only the rematch drops it, to 20 or 12 at high mercy (obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:328-335, gated on `i_ex(obj_lanino_rematch_enemy)`).

OTHER FIGHTS THAT REUSE THESE OBJECTS (do not confuse them with this roster):
  * REMATCH, encounter 141 (scr_encountersetup.gml:1266-1287, enemies at lines 1273 and 1277): obj_lanino_rematch_enemy + obj_elnina_rematch_enemy + obj_elnina_lanino_rematch_controller. Different chooser — obj_elnina_lanino_rematch_controller_Step_0.gml:21-31 picks `attack_chosen` with `choose()` from the three weathers that are not the previous one, and Step_0:375-393 dispatches type 130 with special ALWAYS 0 and difficulty 1/2/3/4 (rain/snow/moon/sun), i.e. it reuses special 0 and varies only the bullet sprite. Its mercy-gated branches (343-366) dispatch type 141, the obj_elnina_bouncingbullet + umbrella turn, and at mercymod 100 (367-370) it just runs a 60-frame empty turn. Its box is a single unconditional create at view +320/+180 (line 308) under `global.mnfight == 1` rather than 1.5.
  * ROUXLS KAARD, encounter 114: obj_lanino_enemy_rouxls / obj_elnina_enemy_rouxls are backup dancers driven from obj_dbulletcontroller type 73 (lines 1256, 1262, 1321, 1324, 1348, 1351) and from obj_room_teevie_chef. Their attacks belong to obj_rouxls_ch3_enemy_Step_0.gml:2894-2942 (types 74, 72, 73, 69, 71, 73.1), NOT here.
  * obj_elnina_umbrella and obj_elnina_bouncingbullet also appear in the Tenna fight (obj_tenna_zoom_Step_0.gml:483-542, obj_tenna_zoom_Other_11.gml:278).
  * obj_elnina_heart and obj_rouxls_raincloud have ZERO references anywhere in Ch3.
engineNeeds:
1. THE CONTROLLER MUST EXIST AND MUST BE THE REPLAY SELF. Both blocks read `turns`: the boxBlock branches on `turns < 7` vs `turns == 7` for the box Y, and the turnBlock is a four-arm ladder on `turns`. Replay them with self = an obj_elnina_lanino_controller instance whose `turns` has been set to the launched attack's turn (1/2 for special 0, 3, 4, 5/6, 7). obj_elnina_mascotattack_Create_0.gml:11-16 and obj_regularbullet_elnina_Step_0.gml:44 also read the live controller, both behind `i_ex()` guards, so a missing controller degrades quietly instead of erroring — which is worse, because it silently drops the forecast bullet sprites and the heart-merge.

2. THE CONTROLLER'S CREATE IS HEAVY AND WILL NEED STUBBING. gml_Object_obj_elnina_lanino_controller_Create_0.gml:44-49 does `instance_create_depth(camerax() + 330, cameray() - 50, -9999999, obj_actor_tenna)`, sets tenna.preset/bounce/sprite_index and calls scr_speaker("tenna"); CleanUp_0 calls safe_delete(tenna); Draw_0:128-135 destroys the controller and stops the music when `global.fighting == 0`. Step_0:169-187 (`intro == 1`) calls `snd_init("rudebuster_boss.ogg")` + `mus_loop_ext`, and the finale reads global.batmusic[0] to fade the music out (obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:250). Either provide obj_actor_tenna and the music globals, or create the controller and immediately force `intro = 4`, `talked = 0`, `turns = <n>` and skip the intro chain.

3. NUMERIC OBJECT INDICES IN A `with`. The dispatcher is `with (_a)` where `_a = 379` (obj_lanino_enemy) or `946` (obj_elnina_enemy) — gml_Object_obj_elnina_lanino_controller_Step_0.gml:1117-1122. The transpiler must resolve a bare integer as an object index (verified against objects.tsv: obj_lanino_enemy is line 381 -> index 379, obj_elnina_enemy line 948 -> 946; the rematch's 993/1591 check out the same way). If the studio spawns the dbulletcontroller manually instead of replaying the block, set `creator`/`creatorid`/`target`/`damage` the way scr_bulletspawner does (gml_GlobalScript_scr_bulletspawner.gml) from a Lanino/Elnina instance, because obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:290-291 copies `obj_dbulletcontroller.target` onto every bullet.

4. PIN DIFFICULTY TO 0. `dc.difficulty` is never written by the main fight, and obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:293-303 uses it as a bullet-SPRITE selector, not a difficulty. A studio DIFF selector of 1-4 will replace the forecast sprites with rain/ice/moon/sun and make the attack look like a rematch turn. controllerSet pins it.

5. THE 850-FRAME TURN IS LOAD-BEARING. Special 4 reads global.turntimer at 500 / 400 / 350 / 250 / 200 / 100 for its dialogue (obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:2629-2746) and at 500 / 350 / 250 / 200 for its shotrate ramp, sprite swap and music fade (obj_elnina_mascotattack_Step_0.gml:243-263). Any studio floor shorter than 850 skips straight past the ramp and the attack fires at a constant rate forever. Note scr_turntimer only RAISES, and the base `scr_turntimer(90)` at Step_0:1062 sits OUTSIDE the sliced turnBlock — harmless here, since every ladder value (260/275/850) is larger.

6. SPRITES ARE REFERENCED BY RAW INDEX. obj_elnina_mascotattack_Create_0.gml:27-48 builds bs[0..5] = 429/3812/4150/4065/4417/1359 (spr_ch3_bullet_raincloud / _ice / _heart / _sun / _moon / _raindrop) and ms[0][0..7] = 472/2176/3561/187/4196/2807/539/1126 (spr_ch3_mascot_moon_* — normal, kiss, large_smug, huge_gloat, scared, chase, chase_small, large_smug_sad) and ms[1][0..7] = 2069/4612/714/4573/4261/4393/266/2595 (the spr_ch3_mascot_cloud_* equivalents). The forecast comparisons use 783/1474/4255/1650 (spr_weather_sun/_moon/_rain/_snow) as bare numbers too (Step_0:307-320, controller Step_0:242-246 and 864-880). All 26 must resolve through the Ch3 sprite index table or the mascots draw blank and the sprite-swap comparisons silently fail.

7. MASCOTS ARE obj_marker INSTANCES. scr_dark_marker(x, y, sprite) creates obj_marker at 2x with image_speed 0 (gml_GlobalScript_scr_dark_marker.gml). They are not bullets and must not be collidable; the attack's CleanUp destroys both (obj_elnina_mascotattack_CleanUp_0.gml). obj_elnina_mascotattack_Draw_0.gml is a bare `exit;`.

8. BULLET-VS-BULLET COLLISION IS MANUAL AND SELF-DIRECTED. obj_regularbullet_elnina_Step_0.gml:31 uses `collision_rectangle(..., object_index, true, true)` — a same-object query with an inflated bbox — then mutates BOTH instances (sprite_index and image_blend, or mutual instance_destroy plus a scr_marker/scr_lerp_var_instance shrink-ball). The engine needs collision_rectangle against `object_index` with the notme flag, and scr_doom / scr_lerpvar_instance / scr_lerp_var_instance / scr_script_delayed, which the mascot and the bullets both lean on heavily.

9. THINGS THAT ARE NOT ATTACKS AND SHOULD NOT BE SPECCED AS SUCH. The whole ACT layer (renaming S-Action/R-Action to "ILoveTV", the ilovetv counter, the 30-cap, sunboost), the turn-3 two-option choicer (global.choicemsg[0..1], global.choice, obj_choicer_neo which Step_0:1316 tests for), the turn-4 in-bullet cut-in (extratimer 39/50/100/140), the forecast HUD (Draw_0:33-126, three glass panes with temperature in F or C by `os_get_region()`), the I LOVE TV digit counter (Draw_0:9-31), and the ~1100 lines of ballooncon dialogue that make up over half the controller Step. The studio can run all five bullet attacks without any of it; it just will not look like the show.
